system_description.narrative_title: A fracturing, transactional global order under strain
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, interdependent flux of regional wars, great-power competition, market shocks and governance crises. Immediate dynamics are driven by the US–Iran confrontation and its regional reverberations, the Russia–Ukraine war and European security strains, and the fusion of national security with commercial tech (semiconductors/AI), all feeding energy-market volatility and political instability. Climate tipping points and weakened multilateral processes (COP31) compound systemic stress, while domestic politics and election outcomes reshape states' external postures.
system_description.scope: State and non-state actors; interstate military conflicts and proxy campaigns; alliances and diplomacy; global energy and commodity flows; international markets and major firms (notably tech and oil); intelligence, cyber and hybrid operations; climate governance processes and transnational civil-society actors; domestic politics insofar as they affect foreign policy.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-ecological system (global human civilization interacting with Earth's biophysical limits)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and commodity markets (oil, gas, fuels)
International technology and industrial supply chains (semiconductors, AI)
Regional security complexes (Middle East conflicts; Eastern Europe/Russia–Ukraine)

variables.name: US–Iran regional confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran are locked in a volatile cycle of strikes, covert actions and intermittent diplomacy with regional mediators, shifting the immediate risk of wider Middle East escalation and complicating deterrence calculations.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain engaged in intense conventional and asymmetric combat as battlefield offensives, strategic strikes and sustained Western/NATO support continuously reshape territorial control and alliance burden-sharing.

variables.name: US–China high‑tech competition
variables.description: The United States and China are escalating strategic competition over semiconductors, AI and information security, with espionage allegations, export controls and legislative pressure recalibrating corporate governance and global supply chains.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure and market volatility
variables.description: Attacks on energy infrastructure, pipeline strikes and refinery disruptions by a mix of state and non‑state actors are driving acute volatility in oil and fuel markets and prompting new security measures along major shipping and transit routes.

variables.name: European hybrid and cyber threats
variables.description: European states face a rising wave of hybrid tactics — including coordinated bomb hoaxes, cyber intrusions and disinformation campaigns by hostile external actors — forcing accelerated changes in intelligence sharing, resilience and law‑enforcement cooperation.
